section.title: De-hyphenation and re-tokenizing term vectors
section.para: DehyphenationCharSequenceNormalizer joins words split at a line break, such as "litiga-\ntion" to "litigation". A letter must precede the hyphen and follow the break, with optional horizontal whitespace before the continuation. The supported hyphens are U+002D, U+00AD and U+2010. The non-breaking hyphen U+2011 is excluded.

Breaks use UnicodeWhitespace.lineBreaks(): U+000A, U+000B, U+000C, U+000D, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029. CRLF counts as one break. Additional breaks prevent a join, so "litiga-
 Page 3
tion" is unchanged. No dictionary is used: a compound split at a hyphen, such as "well-
known", becomes "wellknown".

opennlp.tools.termvector.RetokenizingTermVectorAnnotator tokenizes normalized text and groups terms in tokenizer output order. Unlike TermVectorAnnotator, it does not use an existing token layer, so a joined word can become a single term. Existing layers and document text are preserved. Empty token spans are omitted in both modes. Full mode includes original-text occurrence spans; scoring-only mode includes counts without spans. Offsets use UTF-16 code units.
